newsitem.title: ITALY: Separatists interrupt main Italian television news.
newsitem.headline: Separatists interrupt main Italian television news.

text.p: Police opened an investigation on Tuesday into how state television's main news broadcast was interrupted on Monday by a man urging people in northeast Italy to overthrow the government.
The unknown separatist managed to block out the sound on RAI Uno's evening news show in the northeastern Veneto region twice in 20 minutes and broadcast his own recorded message.
"Now is the time to rise up against the Italian state," the mystery voice said. "The Veneto is a European nation. We Venetians are tired of paying, tired of keeping quiet, tired of being oppressed."
Police said they believed the message was broadcast from the heart of this lagoon city but they did not know how RAI's audio signal was blacked out.
The separatist Northern League party declared independence for the north of Italy in Venice last year, but denied it had anything to do with Monday's stunt.
The Venetian Republic ruled for 14 centuries but lost its independence in 1797, when the French took control. Venice became part of unified Italy at its birth in 1861.
